# A slot's name is the author's and is what a caller writes, so `sngl doc` has
# to say it. It is also an `ast.Param` like a prop, which is what makes the
# `! stdout` lines here worth having: the schema carried Props, Events and a
# Children *type* and no slots at all, so `children` was nameless -- and the
# first fix that gave slots a name gave them one in the Properties table.

# A plain container: the rest slot is named, its `...` visible, and it is not
# a property.
sngl doc vbox
stdout '## Slots'
stdout 'children +\.\.\.component'
stdout '\*\*Children:\*\* many'

# `scroll` bounds the bare children to one. Both halves of that show: the
# slot's own type carries the bound, and the children line stops claiming
# "many", which it said for every component that accepted any children at all.
sngl doc scroll
stdout 'content +\.\.\.component tr\.one'
stdout '\*\*Children:\*\* exactly one'

# A slot that accepts a segmented tree names it.
sngl doc canvas
stdout 'shapes +\.\.\.component shape'

# A component with no rest slot has no Slots section and no children.
sngl doc text
! stdout '## Slots'
stdout '\*\*Children:\*\* none'

# Addressable on its own, and answered as a slot rather than as an event --
# which is what everything that is not a prop used to be called.
sngl doc sngl:ui vbox.children
stdout 'vbox.children \(slot\)'
stdout 'Type: \.\.\.component'
! stdout 'event'

# A scoped slot's parameters are contract, not documentation, so the names are
# printed alongside their types. No stdlib component declares one, so this is
# the local-declaration path.
sngl doc . table
stdout '## Slots'
stdout 'cell +component\(row Row\)'
stdout 'body +...component'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

struct Row {
    title string
}

component table(rows list<Row>, cell component(row Row), body ...component) {
    vbox {
        for var r = rows {
            cell(r)
        }
        body
    }
}

component main {
    table(rows=[]) {
        component cell(r) {
            text(value=r.title)
        }
    }
}
